problems.quote: Polymerase Chain Reaction was invented by Kary Mullis in 1985 (Nobel Prize, 1993).
problems.problem: PCR was invented in 1983, not 1985.
problems.correction: Polymerase Chain Reaction was invented by Kary Mullis in 1983 (Nobel Prize, 1993).
problems.verifierReason: Invention conceived in 1983; 1985 is publication/patent year.

problems.quote: After n cycles, the target sequence is amplified to approximately 2 n copies.
problems.problem: The amplification formula is 2^n, not 2n.
problems.correction: After n cycles, the target sequence is amplified to approximately 2^n copies.
problems.verifierReason: PCR amplification is exponential (2^n), not linear (2n).

problems.quote: DNA polymerase III (leading strand) and DNA polymerase I (lagging strand Okazaki fragment processing)
problems.problem: These polymerase names are specific to bacterial replication; eukaryotic replisomes use Pol ε and Pol δ for leading and lagging strands, not Pol III and Pol I.
problems.correction: In bacteria, DNA polymerase III (leading strand) and DNA polymerase I (lagging strand Okazaki fragment processing); in eukaryotes, Pol ε and Pol δ perform these roles.
problems.verifierReason: Original quote presents bacterial polymerases as universal fact; correction accurately specifies bacterial vs eukaryotic roles.

problems.quote: Therapeutic antibodies (abciximab, eptifibatide) targeting αIIbβ3
problems.problem: eptifibatide is a cyclic peptide inhibitor, not an antibody
problems.correction: Therapeutic agents (abciximab, eptifibatide) targeting αIIbβ3
problems.verifierReason: Eptifibatide is a cyclic heptapeptide GPIIb/IIIa antagonist, not an antibody; abciximab is a chimeric mAb fragment. 'Agents' correctly covers both.

problems.quote: k_cat values up to 10 min⁻¹
problems.problem: The reported k_cat values for the Tetrahymena group I intron and RNase P RNA component are significantly lower (typically 0.01–1 min⁻¹), not up to 10 min⁻¹.
problems.correction: k_cat values up to 1 min⁻¹
problems.verifierReason: Original overstates k_cat; wild-type Tetrahymena group I intron and RNase P RNA typically ≤1 min⁻¹ under standard conditions.

problems.quote: the 531‑kb genome of Mycoplasma genitalium
problems.problem: Wrong genome size and species: Mycoplasma genitalium genome is ~580 kb; the 531‑kb genome refers to JCVI‑syn3.0 (minimized Mycoplasma mycoides). The first synthetic cell (JCVI‑syn1.0) used the 1.08‑Mb Mycoplasma mycoides genome.
problems.correction: the 1.08‑Mb genome of Mycoplasma mycoides
problems.verifierReason: M. genitalium genome is ~580 kb; 531 kb refers to JCVI-syn3.0 (minimized M. mycoides). JCVI-syn1.0 used 1.08 Mb M. mycoides genome.

problems.quote: transplanted it into a Mycoplasma capricolum recipient, and produced a viable cell designated JCVI‑syn1.0
problems.problem: The transplant of the M. genitalium genome did not yield a viable cell; JCVI‑syn1.0 was produced by transplanting the synthetic M. mycoides genome into M. capricolum.
problems.correction: transplanted the synthetic Mycoplasma mycoides genome into Mycoplasma capricolum, producing JCVI‑syn1.0
problems.verifierReason: M. genitalium genome transplant did not yield viable cell; JCVI-syn1.0 resulted from synthetic M. mycoides genome transplant into M. capricolum.

problems.quote: a 473‑kb genome retaining only 473 genes
problems.problem: JCVI‑syn3.0 has a 531‑kb genome (not 473 kb) with 473 genes.
problems.correction: a 531‑kb genome retaining only 473 genes
problems.verifierReason: JCVI-syn3.0 genome is 531 kb with 473 genes, not 473 kb.

problems.quote: the construction of nitrogen‑fixing cereals by transferring the nif gene cluster into a plant‑compatible vector
problems.problem: Nitrogen‑fixing cereals have not been constructed; this is a research goal, not an achieved application.
problems.correction: efforts to engineer nitrogen‑fixing cereals by transferring the nif gene cluster
problems.verifierReason: Nitrogen-fixing cereals have not been constructed; transferring nif cluster remains a research goal.

problems.quote: more flexible than USA (dual amendment process for federal matters only)
problems.problem: The US Constitution does not have a 'dual amendment process for federal matters only'; it has a single amendment process (two methods of proposal and two of ratification) applicable to all amendments.
problems.correction: more flexible than USA (which has a single, rigorous amendment process requiring two-thirds of Congress and three-fourths of states)
problems.verifierReason: US Art. V provides single amendment process with multiple modes, not dual process for federal matters only.

problems.quote: both were constitutional amendments because they modified the First Schedule
problems.problem: The 35th Amendment (1974) did not modify the First Schedule; it added Article 2A and the 10th Schedule for Sikkim as an associate state. Only the 36th Amendment modified the First Schedule.
problems.correction: the 35th Amendment (1974) made Sikkim an associate state, and the 36th Amendment (1975) made it a full state by modifying the First Schedule
problems.verifierReason: 35th Amdt added Art 2A & 10th Schedule for associate state; 36th Amdt amended First Schedule for full statehood.

problems.quote: North-Eastern Areas Reorganisation Act 1971 (Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, Arunachal)
problems.problem: Nagaland became a state in 1963, not through the 1971 Act. The 1971 Act created Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura as states and Mizoram, Arunachal as UTs.
problems.correction: North-Eastern Areas Reorganisation Act 1971 (Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, Arunachal)
problems.verifierReason: Nagaland statehood 1963 via State of Nagaland Act; 1971 Act created Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, Arunachal.

problems.quote: The Supreme Court in State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1963) held that Parliament has the power to cede territory to a foreign country, but this requires a constitutional amendment (as held in t
problems.problem: The holding that cession requires a constitutional amendment comes from the Berubari Union case (1960), not the State of West Bengal case (1963). The latter dealt with Parliament's plenary power over territory.
problems.correction: The Supreme Court in Berubari Union case (1960) held that cession of territory requires a constitutional amendment. In State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1963), the Court held that Parliament has
problems.verifierReason: Berubari (1960) held cession needs constitutional amendment; West Bengal (1963) dealt with Parliament's territorial power.

problems.quote: The term was coined by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle , who is called the Father of Taxonomy.
problems.problem: Augustin Pyramus de Candolle coined the term 'taxonomy', but Carolus Linnaeus is called the Father of Taxonomy.
problems.correction: The term was coined by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle; Carolus Linnaeus is called the Father of Taxonomy.
problems.verifierReason: De Candolle coined 'taxonomy' (1813); Linnaeus is universally recognized as Father of Taxonomy.

problems.quote: Smallest living cells (0.1-0.3 m).
problems.problem: The unit should be micrometers (µm), not meters (m).
problems.correction: Smallest living cells (0.1-0.3 µm).
problems.verifierReason: 0.1-0.3 m is 10-30 cm; smallest cells (Mycoplasma) are 0.1-0.3 µm (100-300 nm).

problems.quote: replicating molecules to chromosomes
problems.problem: The first major transition described by Maynard Smith and Szathmáry is the origin of compartments (protocells), not directly to chromosomes; chromosomes are the second transition.
problems.correction: replicating molecules to compartments (protocells)
problems.verifierReason: First transition is replicating molecules → compartments (protocells); chromosomes are second transition.

problems.quote: cultural to technological evolution
problems.problem: The eighth transition in Maynard Smith and Szathmáry's list is primate societies to human societies (language), not cultural to technological evolution.
problems.correction: primate societies to human societies (language)
problems.verifierReason: Eighth transition is primate societies → human societies (language); cultural/technological evolution is not a listed transition.

problems.quote: excess of male‑biased genes on the X
problems.problem: In Drosophila, the X chromosome is depleted of male-biased genes (demasculinized), not enriched.
problems.correction: paucity of male‑biased genes on the X
problems.verifierReason: Drosophila X chromosome is demasculinized (paucity of male-biased genes), not enriched.

problems.quote: Not available for preventive detention under PD Act (only available for punitive detention).
problems.problem: Article 22 contains specific protections for preventive detention in clauses (4)-(7); only clauses (1)-(2) are inapplicable to preventive detention.
problems.correction: Clauses (1)-(2) not available for preventive detention; clauses (4)-(7) provide safeguards for preventive detention.
problems.verifierReason: Original quote incorrectly implies Art 22 has no protections for preventive detention; Art 22(4)-(7) provide specific safeguards.

problems.quote: Borrowed from Spanish Constitution (name "Directive Principles").
problems.problem: Directive Principles were directly borrowed from the Irish Constitution; the Irish Constitution had borrowed the idea from the Spanish Constitution.
problems.correction: Inspired by Irish Constitution (which borrowed from Spanish Constitution).
problems.verifierReason: DPSP directly borrowed from Irish Constitution (1937), not Spanish (1931); Irish version borrowed from Spanish.

problems.quote: Articles 13, 32, 131-136, 143, 226, 227, and 246 of the Constitution
problems.problem: Article 246 deals with distribution of legislative powers (Union, State, Concurrent Lists), not judicial review. Judicial review is not explicitly provided in Article 246.
problems.correction: Articles 13, 32, 131-136, 143, 226, and 227 of the Constitution
problems.verifierReason: Article 246 distributes legislative powers; it is not a judicial review provision.

problems.quote: The 22nd Law Commission (2015-2018) focused on strengthening the subordinate judiciary and reducing pendency.
problems.problem: The 22nd Law Commission was constituted in 2020; the commission serving 2015-2018 was the 21st Law Commission.
problems.correction: The 21st Law Commission (2015-2018) focused on strengthening the subordinate judiciary and reducing pendency.
problems.verifierReason: The 21st Law Commission served 2015-2018; the 22nd was constituted in 2020.
